title: Why a geometric series cancels itself
subtitle: Geometric Series · Grade 10

voice.name: Fola
voice.style: Friendly, warm, encouraging mathematics teacher; expressive but never theatrical. Natural neutral English, unhurried and conversational, with gentle pauses after numbers and mathematical reasoning. No background music.

beats.narration: How can we add one, two, four, and eight quickly? There is a pattern hiding here.
Each term is double the previous one. That fixed multiplier, two, is called the common ratio.
Call the sum S. So S equals one plus two plus four plus eight.
Double every term. Two S equals two plus four plus eight plus sixteen. Notice how the terms shift.
Align the doubled sum and the original. Two, four, and eight now match, column for column.
Subtract S from two S. The three matching terms cancel. Sixteen minus one remains. Since two S minus S equals S, the sum is fifteen.

The same idea works with any first term a and ratio r. Multiply by r and subtract. For n terms, the sum is a times the bracket r to the power n minus one, all divided by r minus one. But r must not equal one.
Your turn. Add one, three, nine, and twenty-seven. Multiply the sum by three, then subtract. Which terms cancel? Pause and try it yourself.
Three S equals three plus nine plus twenty-seven plus eighty-one. Subtract S. Two S equals eighty-one minus one, which is eighty. So S equals forty. That's the shortcut.
